availability: 已载入保存的 KB 快照、实验记录与评测结果。
flow: ① 解题：默认完整简洁 KB，science 按需展开；每题使用冻结版本，答案尚未揭示。
② 发现：揭示答案，提出可检查的规律与研究问题。
③ 总结与研究：持久任务，40 分钟后标记为下轮延续成员，原任务继续。
④ 下一轮：使用最新已保存并应用的报告版本；每次应用记录所属与应用轮次。

K1001.mechanism: Every candidate is under-trained, so loss falls monotonically with how far parameters move from init; adaptive optimizers move ~lr per step regardless of gradient scale, so lr·T measures distance. Predicts the rule saturates once Δ is enough to fit the (tiny, noiseless) train set (~0.1-0.3), after which overconfidence/overshoot dominates - observed in the phase table.
K1001.phase: Largest-Δ (≥3× gap) win rate depends on the smaller Δ: <0.03 ~95% (tabular lab 2011/2135); 0.03-0.1 ~60-88%; once smaller Δ≥0.1 only 25-60% (bigram 25%, tabular 43%, spiral 54%, multivariate 56%, XOR 58%, univariate 60%; K1012, K1021). LR-ceiling breaks: K1004.

K1004.mechanism: RMSprop's first steps are lr/sqrt(small square-avg) ≈ up to 10× lr with no momentum smoothing; in unnormalized MLPs these kicks inflate hidden activations and the MSE output, so training oscillates. LayerNorm bounds hidden scale (and residual paths keep the function near-identity), absorbing the kicks — predicts instability only when the RMSprop net lacks LN/residual, as observed (6/6 vs 4/8).
K1004.phase: RMSprop≥3e-3 vs ≥3× smaller-Δ choice on MSE: RMSprop net has higher LN+residual score → wins 6/6; equal → 12/22; lower → 4/8. RMSprop 1e-3 univariate 1/4.

regime.note: (a) corpus regression pairs; (b) bigram post-LN transformer vs GRU

K1006.mechanism: Each unnormalized pre-activation layer shrinks hidden RMS (~0.5x for SiLU/GELU at init), so an under-trained deep stack feeds a weak signal to the head; pre-LN restores unit scale and identity paths keep gradient flow, speeding an under-trained net 2-3x. Predicts the LN advantage shrinks once Δ is large enough to learn the scale (tabular Δ>=0.1 reverses, K1009) and where LN destroys label-relevant norm information (2-D spiral, K1020).
K1006.phase: LN-count win rate: multivariate 61-11, univariate 57-12 (lab same-residual more-LN: multivariate at 32768 samples 8/9, ratio 0.38; univariate 37/39), tabular Δ<0.1 41-4 but Δ>=0.1 less-LN 17-6 (K1009); residual at equal LN is the weakest term (lab regression 19/29, ratio ~0.96; q_ca0dea plain beat its residual twin); spiral: K1020; XOR plain+LN vs residual 6/10.

regime.note: tabular only when Δ<0.1; spiral handled by K1020; same optimizer/lr/T

K1008.mechanism: SiLU/GELU have slope ~0.5 near 0 (silu(x)≈x/2), so each un-normalized block halves signal and gradient; stacked smooth blocks attenuate more under small-step optimizers (SGD ratio ~2-5 vs Adam ~1.1, Adam rescales gradients). LN restores scale, which is why an extra LN outweighs the activation (17/33). Predicts the penalty grows with depth and with SGD, and vanishes with per-layer normalisation of every block.
K1008.phase: Rect vs smooth (multivariate lab): equal LN SGD 13/15, adaptive 24/37; rect with fewer LN 17/33 (coin flip); rect with more LN 12/13. Univariate activation-only: ≥2 LN adaptive 9/9, SGD 5/6; <2 LN adaptive 3/6.

regime.note: equal LN count required

K1009.mechanism: With 1024 rows and labels set by 2-4 coordinates, once Δ≥0.1 the decision boundary is already fit; test CE is then set by logit scale on misclassified points, so anything that speeds fitting (depth, LN, ReLU kinks, larger lr) inflates confidence. Predicts the same reversal for optimizer Δ (K1021) and no reversal on XOR/spiral where the boundary is still being learned.
K1009.phase: Δ_shared<0.1: more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17; Δ_shared≥0.1: shallower 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth act 16/16 (counterexample q_87182b: more early LN in residual LeakyReLU won). Across Δ (mixed questions) prefer Δ≈0.1-0.3 over ≥3× larger (K1021).

regime.note: 1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features; Δ per core rule

K1012.phase: Saturation (smaller Δ≥0.1, larger ≥3×; lab): larger-Δ wins bigram 4/16, tabular 63/146, spiral 54%, multivar 56%, XOR 58%, univar 60%. SGD vs adaptive (lab, calibrated Δ): SGD 1-3× behind but ≥2 more LN wins 90/130; 3-10× behind 61/181; 10-30× 25/95 (vs 19% / 13% without the LN edge).

K1018.mechanism: With many distractor coordinates and only ~1024 rows, once the XOR interaction is learned (Δ≥0.05) further capacity of deep LN'd stacks is spent fitting distractor-dependent features and sharpening confidence near the axes, raising test CE; a shallow wide smooth net fits the 2-coordinate product with fewer composed nonlinearities. Predicts the reversal vanishes for ≤4 features (no distractors) or Δ<0.05 (boundary not yet learned) — both observed.
K1018.phase: nf≥8: Δ≥0.05 smooth 15/16, more-LN 8/32, shallow vs ≥3 deeper 5/5; Δ<0.05 more-LN 33/41, shallow 4/14, smooth 3/8. nf<8: Δ≥0.05 more-LN 4/8, deeper 7/7 corpus + 2/2 lab; Δ<0.05 more-LN 8/11.

regime.note: small n (≈4 questions); train rows 1024

K1020.mechanism: Each LN rescales block activations to unit RMS, raising the effective step size of the features that bend the boundary; a skip connection preserves the input path but does not speed feature learning. Predicts LN count dominates whenever learning curved features is the bottleneck (most Δ), and residual matters only when plain deep stacks overshoot (high Δ, harder spirals).
K1020.phase: Plain(more LN) vs res(fewer LN), 0.03≤Δ<0.5: depth gap ≤1 → plain 58/66; res ≥2 deeper → res 6/8 (+q_40922b), corpus 0/1. Δ<0.03 res 14/24; Δ≥0.5 res 5/6. Res(0 LN) vs plain(≥1 LN): Δ<0.5 plain 51/59; ≥0.5 res 10/13.

regime.note: Δ = core-rule units; 0.1-0.5 and ≥0.5 bands have only 3-5 lab sets

K1022.mechanism: A pre-LN right before the last hidden Linear restores unit feature scale feeding the head, so tiny updates (Δ<0.1) move the output more; each unnormalized block after it shrinks hidden RMS (~0.5x for SiLU/GELU). Predicts the advantage fades once Δ≥0.1 (feature scale is learned) - observed 3/6. Why univariate/XOR don't follow is unexplained.
K1022.phase: late-LN wins: tabular Δ<0.1 corpus 6/7, lab 3/5; multivariate Δ<0.1 corpus 5/5, lab 1/2; any family Δ>=0.1 3/6; univariate 1/4 corpus + 1/4 controlled; XOR 1/4 corpus, 2/4 lab.

regime.note: equal LN count, equal residual, same optimizer/lr/T; small n, effect ~5-20%

K1033.mechanism: Depth adds composed nonlinear capacity that, with only 1024 rows and 12+ noise coordinates, is spent fitting distractor structure once the data has been revisited many times; the overfit cost scales with epochs, not with Δ alone. So the Δ at which shallow-wide nets overtake deep ones falls as epochs rise (4→32). Predicts: at ≤4 epochs the K1009 Δ≥0.1 threshold holds; at Δ<0.03 nets are still boundary-limited and depth/LN help.
K1033.phase: shallow(2-block) vs deep(4-block), Δ 0.03-0.1: 32 epochs → shallow 16/16 (ratio .59-.75); 4 epochs → 4/8 (.99). Corpus ≥16 epochs: Δ≥0.1 shallow 12/15 (.65); Δ<0.03 shallow 6/17 (1.04).

regime.note: one instance per family; depth confounded with width/LN; piecewise untested

K1038.mechanism: SGD's step is the raw gradient, so its true displacement scales with the backpropagated gradient magnitude. With PyTorch default init (weight std≈1/√(3·fan_in)) each unnormalized block shrinks activations and hence hidden-layer gradients geometrically, so |g|≈0.01 overestimates Δ for deep plain stacks. LayerNorm restores unit-RMS activations per block, and Adam-family divide by √v, so both are insensitive. Predicts: collapse grows with depth, absent with ≥1 LN or adaptive optimizers.
K1038.phase: SGD larger-Δ win rate: ≥1 LN 88% (493/563); 0 LN depth≤2 rect 80% (77/96), smooth 67% (60/90); 0 LN depth≥3 35% (21/60). Regression 0-LN 53% (37/70); classification 0-LN 69%.

regime.note: SGD net vs rival with >=3x smaller calibrated Δ, rival Δ<0.1; lab within-set pairs

K1039.mechanism: SiLU'(0)=0.5, so each block halves small-signal gradients; LN fixes forward scale but not this derivative attenuation. SGD has no per-parameter rescaling, so the attenuation directly shrinks effective step size, compounding with depth; Adam's 1/√v undoes it. Predicts: effect grows with SiLU depth (5>4 blocks), vanishes under Adam-family, and cannot overcome a large normalization deficit where LN itself is needed (≥2 LN gap on oscillatory sums).
K1039.phase: Rectifier (fewer LN) vs SiLU/GELU (more LN), shared SGD regression: LN gap 0 → 17/18; gap 1 → 14/17; gap ≥2 → 12/25 (corpus 1/6; controlled offset target 6/6, trig 4/12). Adam-family: SiLU-more-LN wins 11/16 (corpus).

K1040.mechanism: torch Adam adds wd·w to the gradient before dividing by √v. Once the spiral is fit, data gradients→~0, so the decay term dominates both numerator and v and Adam takes ~lr-sized normalized steps toward zero, capping weight norm and logit margin (CE floor ~1e-3). AdamW shrinks by lr·wd·w (~1e-6/step), negligible. Predicts harm grows with wd, lr and T, and vanishes when data gradients stay large (noisy-label bigram LM, under-trained 3-turn spirals).
K1040.phase: AdamW(wd) vs Adam(coupled wd), same lr/net, spiral: wd1e-3 ratio ~0.03, wd1e-2 ~0.002 (12/12). β2 .999 vs .95 (same wd): lr 3e-3 ratio 5.8, 1e-3 24 (0.95 wins); lr 3e-4 ratio 0.36 (0.999 wins); with LN signs mixed.

regime.note: one controlled architecture + q_6a81f1, q_682517; RMSprop/Adagrad coupled wd untested; 2-3 turn spirals untested
delta = core-rule displacement (Adam/RMSprop lr*T, Adagrad 2lr*sqrt(T), SGD calibrated)

K1057.phase: Adam wins vs RMSprop by RMSprop/Adam lr ratio: 0.03-0.1: 18/21; 0.3: 18/20; 1: 21/24; 3-3.3: 12/14; 10: 7/7; 33: 2/2; corpus 100×: 0/1. Multivariate: 10/18 (no rule).

regime.note: lab mostly T=256, widths 64-192

K1059.mechanism: Under small SGD steps, update size scales with gradient magnitude; unnormalized ReLU/SiLU blocks after the last LN contract activations and backpropagated gradients, so the head and late layers barely move. Adaptive optimizers rescale per-parameter steps and largely cancel this attenuation, which predicts the much weaker edge under Adam/Adagrad (observed 0.92-0.99 ratios).
K1059.phase: terminal-LN wins (nonresidual, depth≥2, classification): SGD 31/31 (0.69); Adam 70/102 (0.92); RMSprop 7/8; AdamW 6/11 (1.00); Adagrad 21/35 (0.99). Fewer-total-LN case: SGD 11/11, Adam 9/15.

K1061.mechanism: An unnormalized final block after LN'd blocks re-shrinks/attenuates features right before the head, so the plain net's earlier LNs buy little; a residual path carries signal past it. Predicts: the effect vanishes once the plain tail is LN'd (observed), and weakens at larger Δ where every net trains (observed at Δ≥0.1).
K1061.phase: plain last-noLN: residual wins 26/30 (lab+corpus). plain last-LN: XOR-SGD plain 9/10; spiral-adaptive plain 22/23; spiral-SGD residual 3/3 (+2/2 controlled); tabular plain 12/27 lab, 6/6 corpus. Δ≥0.1 (adaptive): residual ~50% (spiral 6/13) — rule off.

regime.note: residual net has fewer LN than the deep plain net; same optimizer config for both; Δ>=0.1 mixed (spiral residual 6/13)

K1063.mechanism: PyTorch RMSprop has no bias correction and a zero-init square average (alpha 0.99), so early steps are ~lr/sqrt(1-0.99^t) ≈ up to 10× lr, kicking a 1-D smooth fit off its low-MSE basin; the transient matters most at short T, predicting the effect fades at T=1024 (observed: 4/9).
K1063.phase: larger RMSprop lr wins: T=256 w≥128 3/24; T=256 w≤96 2/9; T=1024 w≤96 4/9; multivariate 11/25 (no effect).

regime.note: mostly controlled experiment groups (10); T=1024 narrow nets near coin flip

K1065.phase: Δ≥0.05: deeper plain 1/31; deeper residual gap1-2 8/13, gap≥3 0/4 (+corpus shallow 2/3). Δ<0.05: deeper plain 10/25, deeper residual 14/19.

regime.note: gap>=3 residual evidence is 1 lab set + 3 corpus pairs

K1066.phase: deep residual, more LN: 59/63 (lab+corpus). deep residual, ≤LN: lab 33/43, corpus 0/2. deep plain: lab 75% / corpus 0/7 → use last-LN (K1061).

regime.note: pairs depth<=2 vs depth>=3 under identical optimizer; turns 1-2.5

K1068.phase: Larger d_model wins: Δ<0.02 lab 9/16 Adam-family, SGD 6/6; Δ 0.02-0.1 lab 21/23 + corpus 13/13; smaller wins Δ 0.1-0.5 lab 26/27 + corpus 7/11; Δ≥0.5 lab 10/12 + corpus 5/6.

regime.note: post-LN, d_model 32/64/128

K1069.phase: Fewer heads wins: equal d_ff Δ<0.02 1/2, 0.02-0.5 4/4 (ratio 1.000), ≥0.5 2/2 (1.04); fewer heads with larger d_ff 4/4; fewer heads with smaller d_ff 1/3.

regime.note: heads 2 vs 4; thin evidence (~15 lab pairs, 1 controlled)

K1070.mechanism: PyTorch RMSprop (alpha=0.99) zero-inits its square-average without bias correction, so step t is inflated by 1/sqrt(1-0.99^t): cumulative multiplier ≈1.47 at T=256, 1.24 at 512, 1.12 at 1024, 1.06 at 2048. Under-trained CE rewards extra displacement, so the edge must shrink with T (confirmed) and flip where low loss rewards smooth steps (converged spiral, MSE regression). Adam at 1.5× lr closes the spiral gap at T=256 but not ~8% on tabular: no-momentum noise is a second factor.
K1070.phase: Classification T=256: RMS 14/16 (ratio 1.12-1.31); T=512 2/2; T=1024 lab 1/1, controlled 3/4 (1.01-1.04); T=2048 0/1; converged spiral CE<0.003 Adam 2/2. Multivariate: lr≤3e-4 RMS 4/4, lr≥1e-3 Adam 6/6. Bigram: lr≤3e-4 RMS 4/4; lr≥1e-3 transformer Adam 5/5; GRU high-lr unmeasured. Univariate: Adam ~20/25.

regime.note: regression/LM only at lr<=3e-4; univariate regression excluded

K1071.mechanism: Labels are sampled from P(y|x), so minibatch gradients carry irreducible noise; with a constant lr, once the V×V table is fit further displacement only adds noise-driven parameter jitter and memorisation of the 800 training windows (positions/contexts), raising test CE. More parameters per token (d_model 128) reach that fit point at smaller Δ, so the optimum shifts down with width - predicting d128 < d64 ≈ d32 optimum, as observed.

regime.note: same model within set; V 24-48, alpha 0.8-1.4, 800 windows, bs16; Δ<0.03 rivals: max-Δ applies

K1072.mechanism: Adam-family steps are ≈lr per parameter regardless of gradient size, so the per-step change of the network function grows with fan-in and the number of stacked hidden matrices. A 1-D target on 256 points is fit by a wide multi-layer net within Δ≈0.1; further un-annealed lr-sized steps leave a minibatch-jitter MSE floor growing with lr·width. Predicts: narrow (≤32) or 1-layer nets stay progress-limited (max-Δ wins) and harder multivariate targets push the optimum up - both observed.
K1072.phase: Same net, Δ_hi≥1 vs Δ_lo 0.1-0.5: larger wins w64 0/12, w128 5/18, w256 1/13 (controlled 1/12, corpus 0/5); w≤32 9/16; depth-1 8/8 (corpus 10/10). Δ_lo<0.05: low side wins only if Δ_hi≥5 (lab 3/7). Multivariate: larger wins 10/10 lab, 4/5 corpus.

regime.note: width≤32 or depth 1: max-Δ holds; multivariate excluded

K1073.mechanism: Once the boundary is learned, extra displacement inflates logit norm and fits distractor directions on only 1024 rows; test CE punishes confident errors. Bigger batches over more epochs give cleaner gradients, so each unit of Δ fits training rows faster and the overfit point comes at smaller Δ. Sparse interactions need more movement to find the feature pair (higher optimum); axis-aligned piecewise boundaries keep gaining from sharper logits.
K1073.phase: smooth optimum Δ: E4 ≈0.25, E16 ≈0.08, E32 0.05-0.15. Larger(≥3×) wins: E4 small<0.03 56/56; E16 small≥0.1 smooth 2/2, piecewise 10/10, sparse 0/4; E32 smooth small 0.03-0.1 1/10, ≥0.1 0/5; Δ≥0.5 vs 0.01-0.15 at E32 smooth: low wins 24/28.

regime.note: 1024 train rows, 2-16 features; E=4 is bs16, E=16-32 bs64 (batch confounds epochs); controlled only on width-256 1-layer ReLU+LN net

K1074.mechanism: Curved/oscillatory MSE targets need composed nonlinearities; each LN'd block restores unit-scale activations, so a deep stack keeps gradient and feature scale while composition builds curvature a 1-2 layer net reaches slowly. It is an optimisation-speed effect, so it needs comparable displacement: when deep Δ <1/3 of shallow Δ raw movement dominates (observed flip). Without LN or residuals deep plain stacks attenuate signal (observed losses).
K1074.phase: deep(≥4,≥1 LN) vs shallow(≤2): Δ_deep/Δ_shallow ≥1/3 → deep wins uni 380/461, multi 323/435; <1/3 → shallow wins uni 228/295, multi 159/215.

regime.note: Δ ratio uses K1001/K1019 calibration; deep = depth≥4 with ≥1 LN

K1075.mechanism: Both nets must learn a current-token lookup. When nearly frozen, the GRU's gates pass the input embedding straight to the output, so tiny updates already cut CE, while the transformer must first beat random positional embeddings and attention mixing. Once Δ≥0.02 the transformer's residual stream carries token identity and its FF fits the table faster than a 2-layer non-residual GRU; by Δ≥0.1 post-LN transformers overshoot (K1071), returning the edge to the GRU.
K1075.phase: GRU win rate: Δ<0.02 corpus 8/8, lab 1/2, controlled 5/6; 0.02-0.1 equal/larger-d transformer: lab 1/20, controlled 2-layer GRU 0/9, 1-layer 3/9; GRU d>T d 9/9 obs; 0.1-0.5 8/9; ≥0.5 3/3. Flip between Δ 0.015 and 0.05.

regime.note: alpha 0.8-1.4, V 24-48, L 12-24; GRUs non-residual d32/d64; Δ 0.1-0.5 and ≥0.5 cells small (9, 3 pairs)

[K1001] CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1019), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.
[K1002] Adagrad conversion (any family): because Adagrad's step decays as lr/√t, it matches Adam only when its lr is ~√T/2 (8-23×) larger. Same architecture, lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam ≤3× → Adam/AdamW wins 65/70; =10× → coin flip (4-3); ≥30× → Adagrad wins 9/9. Within Adagrad the larger lr always wins (40/41 pairs; lr=3e-3 is never too big — the decay is a built-in anneal). Adagrad at lr≤1e-4 is effectively frozen (Δ≤0.01) and loses to almost any adaptive choice with lr≥3e-5·√T/2.
[K1003] SGD (all families): plain SGD (momentum 0) at lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8% of its appearances; in LMs embedding rows barely move, CE stays ≈ln V). SGD momentum 0.9 behaves like Adam at ~lr/10: so SGD m=0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 ≈ Adam 1e-4-3e-4 and is a real contender — it beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤3e-5-1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3 (e.g. univariate MSE 6e-5 vs 0.03) — but SGD m=0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr (10× smaller Δ). Family calibration (SGD calibration rule): bigram LM ≈ Adam at lr/30 (weaker), MSE regression ≈ Adam at lr/3 (stronger). Compute Δ with momentum.
[K1004] LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum; zero-init square-avg inflates early steps) is noisy: vs ≥3× smaller Δ it wins only 22/36 corpus pairs, BUT 6/6 when its MLP is better (more LN+residual; q_65db92), 12/22 at equal arch, 4/8 when worse; prefer Adam 3e-3 (loses 2/35) over RMSprop at equal lr. (b) Bigram LMs: Δ optimum 0.1-0.3, d128 post-LN transformer 0.03-0.1 (K1071). (c) MLP classification: lr 3e-3 is safe on XOR/spiral, NOT on 1024-row tabular (optimum Δ shrinks with epochs, K1073). (d) UNIVARIATE regression, multi-layer net width≥64: Adam-family lr·T≥1 overshoots (K1072).
[K1005] Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (same-arch pairs: higher wd 3 wins/10 losses, all within 1%); Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas is a coin flip (5-5); beta2 0.95 vs 0.999 is ~even (7-4). Never let these override a lr·T difference; in rankings, order such near-twins by architecture or leave them adjacent. EXCEPTION — tasks whose CE can reach ~1e-4 (two-spiral 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr≥1e-3): torch Adam with coupled weight_decay≥1e-3 loses to an AdamW or wd=0 twin by 30-500× (K1040, q_6a81f1); β2 there flips with lr, so do not use β2 to explain it.
[K1006] MLP ARCHITECTURE DEFAULT (same optimizer for all choices; regression, XOR, spiral, tabular when Δ<0.1): score = (#LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual, MINUS 1 if a NON-residual depth≥4 net's LAST block has no LN (K1061); pick the highest. Ties: on regression ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, then later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Corpus MLP arch-only hits 74/110 (spiral 12/16, tabular 17/32). More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 multivariate, 57-12 univariate, 41-4 tabular Δ<0.1. Overrides: regression deep vs shallow (K1074); spiral residual ≥2 blocks deeper (K1020); shared-SGD regression rectifier vs SiLU (K1039); XOR ≥8 feat. Δ≥0.05 (K1018, K1065); tabular Δ≥0.1 (K1009/K1073).
[K1008] MSE REGRESSION activation (uni/multivariate): at EQUAL LayerNorm count prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU over SiLU/GELU, even for smooth cubic/sin/cos targets — do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Lab equal-LN multivariate 37/52 (SGD 13/15, MSE ratio ~2; Adam-family 24/37, ratio ~1.1); activation-only univariate Adam-family with ≥2 LN 9/9 (ratio ~14). SiLU is worst (LeakyReLU beat SiLU 7/7 activation-only). Epoch: SiLU/GELU nets ranked last in q_b61944, q_c9738e, q_f2b7b5, q_6495eb. With FEWER LN the rectifier is a coin flip (17/33) — count LN first (K1006); shared SGD see K1039. Flips: tabular classification Δ≥0.1 (K1056), XOR ≥8 features (K1018).
[K1009] Budget × depth reversal on synthetic TABULAR classification (1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features, smooth_additive / piecewise / sparse_interaction rules): when the shared Δ≥0.1 (Δ from the core rule: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2·lr·√T, SGD ~lr·T/(1−m)/100 — NOT raw lr·T for SGD/Adagrad), the boundary is already learned and test CE is set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider nets with GELU/SiLU and fewer LN: shallower wins 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth activation 16/16. When Δ<0.1 the normal rule holds (more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17). This 2-regime rule picks 26/32 tabular arch-only winners. XOR/spiral do NOT reverse.
[K1012] When Δs are close (mixed questions, rankings): a ≥4× Δ gap beats architecture (higher Δ wins 35/40 even vs a net with 2+ more LN/residual). Within ~3×, a clearly better MLP (≥2 more LN blocks/residual) wins 11/19 — treat as a toss-up leaning architecture. Δ also saturates: once both Δ≳0.3, extra Δ wins only ~62% (then use lr-ceiling, tabular-overfit and architecture rules). Rankings: sort by log Δ, then architecture; near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2 / ln V, MSE≈Var(y)) form a tied bottom block — order them by architecture, not small lr differences.
[K1015] Residual × depth × task: on regression, depth helps even without residuals (deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15) because composed nonlinearities are needed for curvature; on classification, depth WITHOUT residual hurts (shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13) while deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14. So for CE tasks never pick a deep (≥4) plain stack over a residual one at the same optimizer; for MSE tasks a deep plain stack with ≥2 LN blocks is still competitive. Deep residual MLPs win 53% of their appearances vs 29% for deep plain.
[K1016] Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).

texts: CORE RULE (all families, T=256-2048 steps; every task here is under-trained): rank choices by cumulative per-parameter displacement Δ. Adam/AdamW/RMSprop: Δ≈lr·T. Adagrad (zero-init accumulator, steps decay ~lr/√t): Δ≈2·lr·√T. SGD: Δ≈lr·T·|g|/(1−m) with raw grad |g|≈0.01 (bigram LM 0.003, MSE regression with momentum 0.03 — K1019), i.e. plain SGD ≈ Adam at lr/100, SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/10. The largest-Δ choice wins 85% of optimizer-only and ~85% of mixed questions (after the lr-ceiling exceptions); a 1.5-3× Δ edge usually beats any architecture advantage. Use architecture rules only to break Δ ties (same optimizer+lr) or in architecture-only questions.

Adagrad conversion (any family): because Adagrad's step decays as lr/√t, it matches Adam only when its lr is ~√T/2 (8-23×) larger. Same architecture, lr_Adagrad/lr_Adam ≤3× → Adam/AdamW wins 65/70; =10× → coin flip (4-3); ≥30× → Adagrad wins 9/9. Within Adagrad the larger lr always wins (40/41 pairs; lr=3e-3 is never too big — the decay is a built-in anneal). Adagrad at lr≤1e-4 is effectively frozen (Δ≤0.01) and loses to almost any adaptive choice with lr≥3e-5·√T/2.

SGD (all families): plain SGD (momentum 0) at lr≤3e-3 is nearly frozen (wins ~8% of its appearances; in LMs embedding rows barely move, CE stays ≈ln V). SGD momentum 0.9 behaves like Adam at ~lr/10: so SGD m=0.9 lr 1e-3-3e-3 ≈ Adam 1e-4-3e-4 and is a real contender — it beats Adagrad ≤1e-3, Adam/RMSprop ≤3e-5-1e-4 and unstable RMSprop 3e-3 (e.g. univariate MSE 6e-5 vs 0.03) — but SGD m=0.9 at lr≤3e-4 loses to Adam/RMSprop at the same lr (10× smaller Δ). Family calibration (SGD calibration rule): bigram LM ≈ Adam at lr/30 (weaker), MSE regression ≈ Adam at lr/3 (stronger). Compute Δ with momentum.

LR-ceiling exceptions to the Δ rule: (a) RMSprop lr≥1e-3 on MSE regression (no momentum; zero-init square-avg inflates early steps) is noisy: vs ≥3× smaller Δ it wins only 22/36 corpus pairs, BUT 6/6 when its MLP is better (more LN+residual; q_65db92), 12/22 at equal arch, 4/8 when worse; prefer Adam 3e-3 (loses 2/35) over RMSprop at equal lr. (b) Bigram LMs: Δ optimum 0.1-0.3, d128 post-LN transformer 0.03-0.1 (K1071). (c) MLP classification: lr 3e-3 is safe on XOR/spiral, NOT on 1024-row tabular (optimum Δ shrinks with epochs, K1073). (d) UNIVARIATE regression, multi-layer net width≥64: Adam-family lr·T≥1 overshoots (K1072).

Second-order optimizer knobs are noise at these budgets: weight decay 0-1e-3 changes loss <1% (same-arch pairs: higher wd 3 wins/10 losses, all within 1%); Adam vs AdamW at equal lr/betas is a coin flip (5-5); beta2 0.95 vs 0.999 is ~even (7-4). Never let these override a lr·T difference; in rankings, order such near-twins by architecture or leave them adjacent. EXCEPTION — tasks whose CE can reach ~1e-4 (two-spiral 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr≥1e-3): torch Adam with coupled weight_decay≥1e-3 loses to an AdamW or wd=0 twin by 30-500× (K1040, q_6a81f1); β2 there flips with lr, so do not use β2 to explain it.

MLP ARCHITECTURE DEFAULT (same optimizer for all choices; regression, XOR, spiral, tabular when Δ<0.1): score = (#LayerNorm'd blocks) + 1 if residual, MINUS 1 if a NON-residual depth≥4 net's LAST block has no LN (K1061); pick the highest. Ties: on regression ReLU/LeakyReLU > GELU > SiLU, then later last-LN (K1022), then greater depth. Corpus MLP arch-only hits 74/110 (spiral 12/16, tabular 17/32). More-LN beats less-LN 61-11 multivariate, 57-12 univariate, 41-4 tabular Δ<0.1. Overrides: regression deep vs shallow (K1074); spiral residual ≥2 blocks deeper (K1020); shared-SGD regression rectifier vs SiLU (K1039); XOR ≥8 feat. Δ≥0.05 (K1018, K1065); tabular Δ≥0.1 (K1009/K1073).

MSE REGRESSION activation (uni/multivariate): at EQUAL LayerNorm count prefer ReLU/LeakyReLU over SiLU/GELU, even for smooth cubic/sin/cos targets — do not pick SiLU/GELU for 'smoothness matching'. Lab equal-LN multivariate 37/52 (SGD 13/15, MSE ratio ~2; Adam-family 24/37, ratio ~1.1); activation-only univariate Adam-family with ≥2 LN 9/9 (ratio ~14). SiLU is worst (LeakyReLU beat SiLU 7/7 activation-only). Epoch: SiLU/GELU nets ranked last in q_b61944, q_c9738e, q_f2b7b5, q_6495eb. With FEWER LN the rectifier is a coin flip (17/33) — count LN first (K1006); shared SGD see K1039. Flips: tabular classification Δ≥0.1 (K1056), XOR ≥8 features (K1018).

Budget × depth reversal on synthetic TABULAR classification (1024 train rows, 2-16 Gaussian features, smooth_additive / piecewise / sparse_interaction rules): when the shared Δ≥0.1 (Δ from the core rule: Adam/RMSprop lr·T, Adagrad 2·lr·√T, SGD ~lr·T/(1−m)/100 — NOT raw lr·T for SGD/Adagrad), the boundary is already learned and test CE is set by overconfidence — prefer SHALLOW (1-3 layers), wider nets with GELU/SiLU and fewer LN: shallower wins 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth activation 16/16. When Δ<0.1 the normal rule holds (more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17). This 2-regime rule picks 26/32 tabular arch-only winners. XOR/spiral do NOT reverse.

When Δs are close (mixed questions, rankings): a ≥4× Δ gap beats architecture (higher Δ wins 35/40 even vs a net with 2+ more LN/residual). Within ~3×, a clearly better MLP (≥2 more LN blocks/residual) wins 11/19 — treat as a toss-up leaning architecture. Δ also saturates: once both Δ≳0.3, extra Δ wins only ~62% (then use lr-ceiling, tabular-overfit and architecture rules). Rankings: sort by log Δ, then architecture; near-chance choices (Δ<~0.005: CE≈ln2 / ln V, MSE≈Var(y)) form a tied bottom block — order them by architecture, not small lr differences.

Residual × depth × task: on regression, depth helps even without residuals (deeper plain beats shallower residual 24-15) because composed nonlinearities are needed for curvature; on classification, depth WITHOUT residual hurts (shallower residual beats deeper plain 19-13) while deeper residual beats shallower plain 33-14. So for CE tasks never pick a deep (≥4) plain stack over a residual one at the same optimizer; for MSE tasks a deep plain stack with ≥2 LN blocks is still competitive. Deep residual MLPs win 53% of their appearances vs 29% for deep plain.

Capacity is not the bottleneck: at these budgets parameter count and width barely predict the winner — do not pick the 'biggest model'. Pairwise larger-params wins only 37/76 on bigram LMs, ~50% on univariate regression; at equal depth wider MLPs are a coin flip on regression (5-5) and only mildly better on classification (7-2). Datasets are tiny but noiseless (256-1024 rows), and every candidate has ample capacity; what differs is how fast the parameters move (Δ) and how well signal propagates (LN, residual, activation). Use width/params only as the last tie-breaker (and prefer wider only in the tabular Δ≥0.1 regime).

Bigram LM transformer SHAPE (transformer vs transformer, same optimizer/lr/T; Δ in core-rule units). EQUAL d_model, layer count: 0.1≤Δ<0.5 FEWER layers wins 23/23 (corpus 6/6, lab 17/17; q_ce881e, q_f2011a); Δ≥0.5 fewer 8/11; 0.02≤Δ<0.1 COIN FLIP (fewer 8/15; q_4f69f2, q_9344eb: 2-layer beat 1-layer) - do not decide by depth there; Δ<0.02 deeper wins 19/28. EQUAL depth: larger d_ff is a tie-break worth ~1-2% CE - wins at Δ≤0.1 (11/12; q_f2011a 256>128>64), not above (3/13). DIFFERENT d_model: 0.02≤Δ<0.1 larger wins 15/15; Δ≥0.5 smaller wins 5/6, order by d_model ascending then layers (q_17f213; K1068). GRU vs transformer: K1075; lr: K1071.

XOR with ≥8 input features (≥6 noise distractors), same optimizer: the architecture rule FLIPS at shared core-rule Δ≈0.05. Δ≥0.05 (e.g. Adam-family lr·T≥0.05): GELU/SiLU beats ReLU/LeakyReLU (lab 15/16, CE ratio 0.78; corpus 6/6); FEWER LayerNorms win (more-LN wins only 8/32 lab, 5/11 corpus); a ≤2-block net beats one ≥3 blocks deeper (lab 5/5, ratio 0.51; corpus 2/3; q_bfba99, q_e914b6). Δ<0.05 (e.g. SGD m0.9 3e-4×1024): normal rule - more LN wins 33/41 (ratio 0.93), deeper beats shallow (shallow 4/14), activation ~coin flip (smooth 3/8). With <8 features keep deeper (7/7); more-LN there is a coin flip at Δ≥0.05 (4/8). Depth×residual: K1065.

SGD gradient-scale calibration for the Δ rule (K1001 assumes raw |g|≈0.01), fit on 368 SGD-vs-adaptive pairs. Bigram LM: use |g|≈0.003 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/30, plain ≈ lr/300): larger-Δ correct 68/70 vs 63/70 at 0.01; SGD m=0.9 beat Adam/AdamW/RMSprop in only 1/18 LM pairs (1/4 even at nominal Δ parity). MSE regression with momentum 0.9: use |g|≈0.03 (SGD m=0.9 ≈ Adam at lr/3): 59/71 vs 54/71; it wins 11/19 when the adaptive Δ is ≤4× its 0.01-estimate. Classification (131/146) and plain-SGD regression: keep 0.01. Plain SGD wins only 3/141 pairs when the adaptive Δ is >15× larger. These calibrations assume the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm; 0-LN SGD nets get far less credit (K1038).

TWO-SPIRAL classification MLPs (same optimizer/lr/T): score LN count FIRST, residual as tie-break - UNLESS the residual net is ≥2 blocks DEEPER. Same residual status: more LN wins (lab 163/206, CE ratio 0.79-0.92). Plain-more-LN vs residual-fewer-LN at 0.03≤Δ<0.5: plain wins when depths are within ±1 (lab 58/66, ratio 0.85; q_31abed), but a residual net ≥2 blocks deeper wins (lab 6/8, ratio 0.71; q_40922b: depth-5 residual, Adagrad 3e-3×1024, beat depth-3 plain nets with more LN; K1066). Δ<0.03: coin flip (residual 14/24). Δ≥0.5: residual 5/6. Residual with ZERO LN loses to plain ≥1-LN nets at Δ<0.5 (lab 8/59), wins at Δ≥0.5 (10/13).

LN PLACEMENT tie-breaker (MLP pre-LN blocks): at equal LN count and equal residual status, prefer the net whose last LayerNorm is closer to the output head (fewer unnormalized blocks after the final LN). Holds on synthetic tabular classification and multivariate regression when Δ<0.1: corpus 11/12 pairs (median loss ratio ~0.80); lab 4/7 (ratio ~0.99); controlled smooth-additive test 2/2 (0.95); q_7ae5d3 (tabular, Adagrad ≤3e-4) agrees. Does NOT hold on univariate regression or XOR (corpus 2/8; controlled univariate 1/4) nor at Δ≥0.1 (3/6). Apply only after LN count + residual tie (K1006); whether late placement beats one extra early LN is untested.

Tabular depth reversal starts EARLIER with more epochs (synthetic tabular classification, 1024 rows, 16 features): at total_samples_seen=32768 (32 epochs, T=512 bs64) shallow 2-block wide nets beat 4-block nets already at Δ≈0.03-0.1 (Adagrad 1e-3×512 Δ0.045, Adam 1e-4×512): controlled sparse_interaction + smooth_additive, shallow wins 16/16 pairings (median CE ratio 0.59-0.75); q_eeb76a (two 2-block 2-LN plain nets 1st-2nd, 4-block 4-LN residual last). At 4 epochs (T=256 bs16) same Δ is a coin flip (4/8, ratio 0.99). Among shallow nets more LN wins (2-LN plain > 1-LN residual 6/6); among deep, residual > plain (6/6, ratio 0.80). Below Δ 0.03 depth still OK (corpus ≥16 ep: shallow 6/17).

SGD Δ credit needs normalization (all MLP families, same set, SGD net has ≥3× the calibrated Δ of K1001/K1019 and rival Δ<0.1): if the SGD net has ≥1 LayerNorm its larger Δ wins 88% (lab 493/563); with ZERO LN only 61% (80/132), and with zero LN + depth≥3 only 35% (lab 21/60, 18 sets; median loss ratio ≈1.0) — treat it as near-frozen and rank it below adaptive/normalized rivals with 3-10× smaller Δ. 0-LN depth≤2: rectifier 80%, smooth 67%; on MSE regression any 0-LN SGD net is a coin flip (37/70). Adaptive optimizers keep 74-89% even with 0 LN. E.g. q_bfe225 (plain SGD 3e-3, 3-layer 0-LN SiLU ranked last), q_1469ce (1-layer 0-LN GELU SGD m0.9 lost to 2-LN RMSprop 3e-5).

SGD × activation on MSE regression (uni/multivariate, all choices share one SGD optimizer, plain or m=0.9, 256-2048 steps): smooth activations (SiLU, GELU) are penalised far more than under Adam, so activation outranks a ONE-block LN deficit. ReLU/LeakyReLU vs SiLU/GELU: equal LN corpus 9/10 + controlled 8/8 (MSE ratio 0.04-0.5); rectifier with 1 fewer LN wins 14/17 (controlled 6/6, corpus 5/8, q_47a7c4, q_4a2253 LeakyReLU 3-LN beat SiLU 4-LN residual); with ≥2 fewer LN only 12/25 (corpus 1/6; wins mainly on large-offset targets) — keep LN count first (K1006). Deeper SiLU nets lose more (depth5 12/16, depth4 4/8). Under Adam-family keep K1006 (corpus: SiLU with more LN wins 11/16).

Spiral coupled weight decay (two-spiral CE, 1-1.5 turns, Adam-family lr 1e-3-3e-3, T≈1024, CE can reach ~1e-4): torch Adam with weight_decay≥1e-3 (L2 coupled into the adaptive gradient) is far worse than AdamW at the same wd or any wd=0 twin: controlled plain ReLU d2 w48 lr 3e-3: Adam wd1e-3 CE 0.003, wd1e-2 0.044 vs AdamW wd1e-3/1e-2 ≤2e-4, wd=0 3e-5-1.8e-4 (AdamW beats Adam 12/12 cells, ratio 0.002-0.03); q_6a81f1 AdamW beat Adam (both wd1e-3) on 1-layer GELU w256. Rank coupled-Adam+wd below such twins regardless of β2. β2 alone flips with lr (0.95 better at lr≥1e-3 plain nets, 0.999 at 3e-4): weak tie-break. Not seen on bigram LM (q_e6d625).

TABULAR classification (synthetic, 1024 rows), once trained (shared core-rule Δ≥0.1, same optimizer/lr/T): prefer GELU/SiLU over ReLU/LeakyReLU. Smooth wins 23/25 lab within-set pairs (~11 sets, median test-CE ratio ~0.80; smooth_additive 14/14, sparse_interaction 5/6, piecewise 4/5); corpus 16/16 (K1009). At Δ 0.01-0.1 only a tendency (44/74, ratio 0.87); at Δ<0.01 no effect (8/19, ratio 1.00) - decide by LN/depth instead. Activation-only matched pairs 19/28. q_b68ab2: plain SiLU RMSprop 1e-4×2048 (Δ0.2) beat residual LeakyReLU nets at larger Δ.

UNIVARIATE regression, same MLP, Adam/AdamW vs RMSprop: Adam-family wins at almost any lr pairing - lab 78/88 same-arch within-set pairs (median MSE ratio ~0.06): equal lr 21/24; Adam at 3-33× LOWER lr 21/23; Adam at 3-10×+ higher lr 36/41. Adam lr≤RMSprop lr subset: non-oscillatory targets 15/15 (ratio 0.02), sin/cos(2πx) targets 27/32 (0.18). Corpus 4/5 (only loss: Adam 3e-5 vs RMSprop 3e-3, 100× gap). Do not credit RMSprop's early-step amplification (q_7f8fb0: AdamW 3e-5 beat RMSprop 3e-5 and 1e-4). Wide-net lr·T≥1 overshoot (K1055) still applies first. NOT multivariate (lab 10/18, ratio 0.97; corpus 5/9).

Classification MLPs (tabular, XOR, spiral), NON-residual, depth≥2, all choices on the same SGD (plain or momentum): the net whose LAST hidden block has LayerNorm wins 31/31 lab within-set pairs (14 sets, median CE ratio 0.69) - even when it has FEWER LayerNorms in total (11/11, ratio 0.76). An unnormalized tail undoes earlier LN (q_1af0fa: a deep net with internal LN but 2 unnormalized final blocks lost to a shallower wider net; normalizing those blocks cut CE 0.69→0.47 in a controlled rerun). With adaptive optimizers the edge is weaker: Adam 70/102 (ratio 0.92), Adagrad 21/35 (~0.99). Regression: univariate 17/25, multivariate 20/35 - not reliable.

CLASSIFICATION MLPs (XOR/spiral/tabular), shared optimizer, Δ<0.1: RESIDUAL net vs NON-residual depth≥4 net with MORE LayerNorms — look at the plain net's LAST hidden block. Last block un-normalized → the residual net wins (lab SGD 16/16, CE ratio 0.72; adaptive 5/9; corpus 5/5): LNs followed by an unnormalized tail don't count. Last block LN'd → family-dependent: XOR+SGD plain wins 9/10; spiral+Adam-family plain wins 22/23 (residual CE ×1.3-1.4); spiral+SGD residual wins (lab 3/3, controlled 2/2, ratio 0.3-0.8); tabular ~coin flip (lab 12/27, corpus 6/6 plain). Moving LN to the last block (same count) lowered plain CE in 6/6 controlled cells.

UNIVARIATE regression, RMSprop vs RMSprop (same MLP, different lr): the LOWER RMSprop lr usually wins, even at small Δ — lab larger-lr wins 9/42 (10 experiment groups; T=256 width≥128: 3/24, median MSE ratio 3.6; lr 1e-4 vs 3e-5: 3/11), corpus 2/3. At T=1024 on narrow nets it is a coin flip (4/9). RMSprop as the larger-Δ choice against Adam/AdamW of the same net also loses (lab 0/21 at RMSprop lr≥3e-4). Do not apply max-Δ to RMSprop on univariate MSE; multivariate is a coin flip (11/25).

XOR with ≥8 input features, once trained (shared optimizer, Δ≥0.05): depth helps only WITH residuals. A deeper NON-residual MLP loses to a shallower one even at a 1-2 block gap (lab deeper wins 1/31, 13 sets, CE ×1.23); a deeper RESIDUAL MLP beats a shallower one at a 1-2 block gap (8/13, 7 sets, CE ×0.82) but loses at gap ≥3 (lab 0/4, corpus 2-vs-5 block 2/3 shallow, K1018). q_164857 (AdamW 1e-4×2048): 3-block residual SiLU nets beat 1-block w192 nets, and the 3-block non-residual GELU net was last. At Δ<0.05 depth is a coin flip (plain 10/25, residual 14/19 deeper wins).

TWO-SPIRAL classification, DEEP vs SHALLOW (same optimizer): a deeper (≥3 block) RESIDUAL MLP with MORE LayerNorms than a shallow (≤2 block) net wins almost always — lab 51/55 (adaptive Δ≥0.05 34/35, CE ratio 0.38; adaptive Δ<0.05 11/14; SGD 6/6, ratio 0.36), corpus 8/8 (ratio 0.76) — even if the shallow net is much wider. Deeper NON-residual nets are unreliable: lab 30/32 with more LN but corpus 0/7 (q_5fe255, q_774f6c had unnormalized last blocks) — credit them only if their last block is LN'd (K1061). Deeper residual with ≤ the shallow net's LN: lab 33/43, corpus 0/2 — tendency only. q_d7ea11: 3-LN residual deep net beat the shallow wide pick.

BIGRAM LM post-LN TRANSFORMER d_model × Δ (same optimizer/lr/T, different d_model): wider wins only while under-trained; the flip is at Δ≈0.1. Δ 0.02-0.1: LARGER d_model wins (lab 21/23, corpus 13/13, CE ratio ~0.98). Δ 0.1-0.5 (e.g. Adam-family 3e-4 at T=512-1024): SMALLER d_model wins (lab 26/27 — d64 beat d128 20/21, d32 beat d128 2/2 with ratio 1.14; corpus 7/11, d64 vs d128 3/3). Δ≥0.5: smaller wins (lab 10/12, corpus 5/6). Δ<0.02: coin flip, SGD favors wider. Fills K1017's gap. q_02539d: d128 AdamW 3e-4×512 (Δ0.15) lost to d64 RMSprop 3e-3×512.

BIGRAM LM post-LN TRANSFORMER head count (same d_model/layers/optimizer/T): fewer heads (2 vs 4) wins 12/15 lab pairs. At Δ<0.5 it is only a tie-break (CE ratio ≈1.00); at Δ≥0.5 it matters (lab 4/4, ratio 1.01-1.07; controlled q_d6dddb d128 AdamW 3e-3×256: 2 heads −0.18 nats vs 4 heads, d_ff 128→256 only +0.07) and head count outranks a 2× d_ff difference (fewer heads + larger d_ff beat more heads + smaller d_ff 4/4). q_d6dddb gold: 2-head d_ff256 beat 4-head d_ff128. Order: d_model/layers (K1017) first, then heads, then d_ff.

CLASSIFICATION MLPs (spiral/XOR/tabular), RMSprop vs Adam/AdamW at the SAME lr, same net, T≤1024: RMSprop usually WINS — lab 17/20 matched pairs (median Adam/RMS CE ratio 1.12; XOR 1.31, tabular 1.20, spiral 1.12), controlled 7/8; epoch q_4c1af8, q_e4c256 (XOR 3e-4, 3e-5), q_ebfdb8 (tabular 1e-4). Treat RMSprop ≈ Adam at ~1.5× lr (Adam at 3.3× lr wins 5/9). Edge shrinks with T (tabular ratio 1.19 at T=256 → 1.04 at 1024; T=2048 Adam 1/1) and vanishes once CE≈0. At lr≤3e-4 also on multivariate regression (4/4) and bigram LM (4/4). At lr≥1e-3 Adam wins: bigram transformer 5/5 (ratio 1.02-1.08; q_a97a96 RMSprop 3e-3 last), multivariate 6/6; univariate regression always Adam (K1057).

BIGRAM LM learning-rate sweet spot (same model; choices differ in optimizer/lr/T; Δ per K1001): past a model-specific optimum MORE Δ LOSES - the solver's most common LM miss. d32/d64 transformers and GRUs: optimum Δ≈0.1-0.3 (Adam-family 3e-4 at T=512-1024, 1e-3 at T=256; Adagrad 3e-3); ≥2× more Δ than a rival already at 0.1-0.3 loses (lab transformer 1/44, GRU 1/6, CE +2-20%); Δ≥1 loses to any rival with Δ≥0.03 (lab 0/17; q_c3a179). d_model=128 post-LN transformer: optimum ≈0.03-0.1; larger loses 0/11 once rival Δ≥0.03 (q_88802d AdamW 3e-3×256 last). Below the optimum max-Δ holds (13/13; GRU 14/15). Corpus: pick 'Δ nearest 0.2 (0.1 for d128)' 52/65 vs max-Δ 43/65.

UNIVARIATE regression lr OVERSHOOT (same multi-layer MLP, depth≥2, width≥64; choices differ in optimizer/lr): Adam/AdamW/RMSprop Δ=lr·T≥1 loses to a Δ≈0.1-0.5 rival (Adam/AdamW 1e-4×1024, 3e-4×512, Adagrad 3e-3): corpus 5/5; lab larger-Δ wins w64 0/12 (MSE ×8.8), w128 5/18 (×5.5), w256 1/13 (×4.4); controlled 11/12. A rival with Δ<0.05 is still undertrained and wins only if the high side has Δ≥5 (q_f609cc: Adam 3e-3 beat Adam 3e-5; lab 3/7). Larger Δ still wins at width≤32 (lab 9/16; q_cdbed5 w16), on depth-1 nets (lab 8/8, corpus 10/10) and on MULTIVARIATE regression (corpus 4/5, lab 10/10).

TABULAR classification Δ sweet spot vs EPOCHS (synthetic, 1024 rows; E=total_samples_seen/1024; core-rule Δ). Below Δ≈0.03 more Δ wins at E=4 (lab 56/56). The CE-optimal Δ then SHRINKS with E on smooth_additive: E=4 ≈0.25 (Δ0.77 lost to 0.26, 3/3 controlled); E=16 ≈0.08 (controlled 2/2; q_c1581a RMSprop 1e-4×256 bs64 Δ0.026 beat Adam 1e-3 Δ0.26 and AdamW 3e-3 Δ0.77); E=32 ≈0.05-0.15: Δ≥0.5 loses (lab 24/28) and ≥3× more loses 1/15 once small Δ≥0.03. sparse_interaction: optimum ≈0.25 at E 4-16, 0.15 at E 32; larger loses once small Δ≥0.1 (lab 5/33, CE ×1.44). piecewise tolerates more (larger wins 10/10 at E=16). Then use architecture (K1009/K1033).

REGRESSION DEPTH (univariate/multivariate MSE MLPs; picking the shallow-wide net is the most common univariate miss): a depth≥4 net with ≥1 LayerNorm (and ≥ the rival's LN count) beats a depth≤2 net - even a wider and/or residual one - whenever its core-rule Δ is ≥1/3 of the shallow net's: univariate corpus 31/38, lab 380/461 (MSE ratio ~0.15-0.2); multivariate corpus 18/22, lab 323/435 (~0.7). If deep Δ <1/3 of shallow Δ the shallow net wins (uni corpus 8/9, lab 228/295; multi 6/6, 159/215). Deeper residual beats shallower non-residual 32-2; deep-narrow beats shallow-wide 70-32. Deep NON-residual 0-LN stacks attenuate signal and usually lose.

BIGRAM LM GRU vs post-LN transformer (same optimizer/lr/T): decide by the shared core-rule Δ band. Δ<0.02 (nearly frozen: Adam-family ≤3e-5 at T≤512, SGD ≤3e-3): GRU wins, even vs larger d_model when alpha≤1 (corpus 8/8, controlled GRU 5/6; q_5e328e GRU64×2 beat d128). 0.02≤Δ<0.1: a transformer of EQUAL or LARGER d_model wins (lab GRU 1/20; controlled 2-layer GRU 0/9 at every T 256-2048; q_9344eb GRU64×2 last at AdamW 3e-5×2048, even below d32×3 d_ff256); GRU64 vs d32: GRU 9/9 observational, lean GRU only if 1-layer. 0.1≤Δ<0.5: GRU wins 8/9 (any d_model). Δ≥0.5: GRU 3/3 (transformer overshoots, K1071).
